claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for, and if so, how many children are there?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 6 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 6 years old and lives with you.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand a bit more about your responsibilities for Alex:

**Are you the person primarily responsible for Alex's care? In other words, are you the one who pays for his food, clothes, and other day-to-day expenses?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I'm the one who looks after him and pays for all his things - his food, clothes, school stuff, everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. One final question:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation, or does he live at home with you full-time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually, he was in care for a little while - just a couple of months earlier this year. But he's back home with me now full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. I need to understand this a bit better:

**How long ago did Alex return home from care, and how long was he in care for in total?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He was in care for 7 weeks in total, and he's been back home with me now for a while.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Good News! ✓

**You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the criteria for claiming Child Benefit for your son:

- ✓ Alex is 6 years old (under 16)
- ✓ You live in the UK
- ✓ Alex lives with you full-time
- ✓ You are responsible for his care and pay for his food, clothes, and other needs
- ✓ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

Regarding Alex's time in care: Since he was only in care for 7 weeks (which is under the 8-week threshold), and he's now back home with you permanently, this does not affect your eligibility.

**Next Steps:**
You can proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit. If you haven't already claimed, you should do so as soon as possible, as Child Benefit can usually only be backdated for up to 3 months.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
